chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ziyad, Abu al-Hasan al-Wasiti, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a group who locked the door upon a bird from the doves of the Haram, so it died. He (peace be upon him) said: Upon them is the price of each bird, half a dirham, by which the doves of the Haram are fed.

key_terms.حَمَامُ الْحَرَمِ: The sacred doves of the Haram (Mecca/Medina)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for a sacred dove of the Haram that dies due to human negligence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific financial compensation (diyah) for a sacred dove of the Haram that dies due to human negligence, establishing a fixed rate of half a dirham per bird. The funds are designated for feeding the remaining flock, reflecting the practical management of the Haram's sanctity and resources in early Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the continuity of pre-Islamic and Islamic traditions regarding the protection of sacred animals within the holy precincts.
